chapter: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
title: Leaving Wooding after hearing the Cotton Pickers
summary: Feeling stale, Cheatham left in Paris, having fallen in love with the McKinney's Cotton Pickers records; Wooding himself felt unaffected by distance from America.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, I came back to the states because I was -- listening a lot of times to this thing -- some recordings, especially Cotton-picker's Band. I fell in love with that band when I was in Europe. I heard them -- some of their recordings and I felt as though I need improvement -- I says, I'm getting stale.
Yes, I was wondering cause I asked Sam about that, you know, I asked him if he didn't feel that he was out of touch --
Being in Europe, and he said he really didn't, he had his own thing going.
